clue.text: Simulated return in public transport

annotationWithheld.why: Simulated return in public transport (5): BOGUS is B(OG)US, but no clue word gives GO to be reversed; 'return' would have to be both the GO and its reversal indicator

clue.text: Happy expression on a Nor folk waterway?

definitions.text: Happy expression on a Nor folk waterway?

parts.words: Happy expression on a Nor folk waterway?
parts.note: a smile seen on one of the wide lakes of eastern England, read as a description of a wide smile

explanation.surface: Someone beams with pleasure while boating in eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a network of shallow lakes and rivers in eastern England; a Broad is one of those lakes, so a grin on it is a broad grin. 'Nor folk' is the newspaper's split of 'Norfolk'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide, open smile is a standard picture of happiness on the face.

clue.text: Bird for the old convict

parts.note: grey hair marks the old, so grey stands for old
a lag is slang for a convict, especially an old lag

explanation.surface: Someone picks out a fitting bird for an elderly prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old lag' is British slang for a hardened ex-convict, which helps the surface hide the split.
explanation.definitionFit: The greylag is a wild grey goose of Europe, ancestor of the farmyard goose.

clue.text: Indicate who's wrong

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of place, so the word before is rearranged

explanation.surface: A demand to point out the person at fault.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to point it out or make it plain.

clue.text: Take my girl and see a resort

indicators.note: take apart is the sense here: the words my girl and see are taken to pieces and reassembled

explanation.surface: An invitation to bring one's girlfriend along and visit the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' is a loose anagram signal, the letters of MY GIRL plus SEE are taken apart and rebuilt. Lyme Regis is a seaside town on the Dorset coast of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyme Regis is a well-known coastal holiday town in Dorset, famous for fossils.

clue.text: How Esau bungled his birthright

parts.note: in Genesis Esau sells his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of stew, the 'pottage' of the Bible story

explanation.surface: A question about the biblical brother who threw away his inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: Esau traded his birthright for 'a mess of pottage'; a mess is an old word for a serving of food, so the phrase for botching something describes the deal literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To botch or ruin something is a common idiom; here the 'mess' is also the dish he took.

clue.text: First sign of dirt engrained in the 1.O.W.

annotationWithheld.why: First sign of dirt engrained in the 1.O.W. (4): RYDE is D inside RYE, but RYE (grain) comes only from 'engrained', which would also have to be the container indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: First sign of dirt engrained in the 1.O.W.

clue.text: Fish the Senior Service watch around for

indicators.note: around says the word for watch is placed round the navy's letters

parts.note: to keep watch is to guard; a guard is also a watch
the Senior Service is the Royal Navy, abbreviated RN

explanation.surface: A sailor wonders which fish the Navy guards.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Navy is called the Senior Service in Britain because it is the oldest of the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The gurnard is a bony-headed sea fish with a large spiny head.

clue.text: Various diets in their place

indicators.note: various suggests different forms, so the letters of diets are rearranged

explanation.surface: A range of eating plans, each set out in its proper spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are sited are located or positioned where they belong.

clue.text: Distressing for one turning sour

indicators.note: turning means the letters of sour are churned into a new order, as milk turns

explanation.surface: Something upsetting about a person going bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning sour' sounds like milk going off; 'turning' is the anagram signal on SOUR, giving ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is burdensome and troubling, weighing heavily on someone.

clue.text: Dish of sterling worth — so private tells Rex, anyway

indicators.note: anyway, meaning in any old order, tells us to rearrange the letters

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: A soldier confides to the king about a valuable piece of tableware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like an adjective or a secret, but it is anagram fodder with TELLS and R; 'anyway' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A silver platter is a large serving plate made of solid silver, sterling quality.

clue.text: French philosopher, one the German found in a spot

indicators.note: found in says the pieces sit inside the word for spot

parts.note: a spot is a dot
one is the Roman numeral I
der is the masculine German word for the

explanation.surface: A French thinker, along with a German, is discovered somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the German' looks like a second person in the scene; it is German's own word for 'the', DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot was an 18th-century French Enlightenment thinker who edited the Encyclopédie.

clue.text: Surrealist about 14 .

indicators.note: about here means turned around in any order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: 14 refers to the answer to 14-across, laid

explanation.surface: A painter is described in terms of another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The three clues 12, 13 and 14 are joined by dots into one sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was the Spanish painter best known for melting clocks and Surrealist imagery.

clue.text: … with whom I transcribe a Greek epic …

indicators.note: transcribe suggests copying out afresh, so the letters are written in a new order

parts.note: whom refers back to the surrealist of 12-across, the painter Dali

explanation.surface: Continuing the chain: the painter and the writer copy out an ancient poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whom' points back to the answer of the previous clue, the painter DALI.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem about the Trojan War is one of the founding works of Greek literature.

clue.text: … arranged to face the other way

indicators.note: this word means the letters it governs are turned round, so they are read backwards
turning to the other way means the word for face is read backwards

parts.note: a clock's face is its dial

explanation.surface: Something set out so as to look in the opposite direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' looks like a verb with 'the other way'; it is a noun, a clock face or dial.
explanation.definitionFit: To have laid things is to have set them out or put them in order, like a table.

clue.text: Nevertheless, I will shortly get under way

indicators.note: in a down answer, get under means one piece sits below the other

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
I will shortened is I'll

explanation.surface: Someone promises to set off soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get under way' reads as starting a journey; in this down clue 'get under' puts I'LL below ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Still, used as an adverb, means all the same or even so.

clue.text: Poe's bird said this, and more

definitions.text: Poe's bird said this, and more

parts.words: Poe's bird said this, and more
parts.note: in Edgar Allan Poe's poem The Raven, the bird's one repeated word is a single word ending in 'more'

explanation.surface: A remark about the famous croaking bird in an American poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The raven's refrain is 'Nevermore'; the clue asks for that word without its 'more'.
explanation.definitionFit: Not ever, at no time: the first half of the raven's word means exactly this.

clue.text: True, my Lord Bishop!

parts.note: a speaker agrees with a bishop, using the formal style by which Anglican bishops are addressed

explanation.surface: A deferential agreement with a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' means true or correct, and the Right Reverend is the formal title of an Anglican bishop, so the answer is both 'correct, your Reverence' and the title itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Right Reverend is the honorific style of a bishop in the Church of England.

clue.text: Male supporter of Women's Lib?

parts.note: a man who backs feminism, reread as a man who is keen on the opposite sex

explanation.surface: A man who champions the feminist movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a political ally of feminism; the answer is a man who chases women and is popular with them.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser who is charming and attractive to women is called this.

clue.text: Sure is an epithet for one so calm

explanation.walkthrough: 'is an epithet for one so' joins the two senses: someone sure of themselves is described by the answer, and so is someone calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in command of one's feelings makes a person both confident and composed.

clue.text: Bung in the hole

parts.note: a plug pushed into a gap, read as anything that temporarily fills a space

explanation.surface: Stuffing a stopper into an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: A bung stops a gap; the answer is any temporary substitute that fills a vacancy.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary measure used until something better is found fills a gap for now.

clue.text: Cob and pen, say, each making port

parts.note: a cob is a male swan and a pen a female one, so the pair are examples of these birds

explanation.surface: A pair of birds, each one heading for a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cob' and 'pen' look like a horse and a writing tool, but they are male and female swans. Swansea is a port city in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city with a harbour on the south Wales shore.

clue.text: Fall for a medical man at work

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for a doctor
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A doctor at the hospital takes a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop is to fall, as from a height or in amount.

clue.text: Profundity, in a measure

definitions.meaning: a dimension measured downward, how far down something goes

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepness is both a quality of serious thought and a dimension measured from the surface downwards.

clue.text: Where Scots have a restriction on loud playing?

parts.note: a ban is a restriction
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud playing

explanation.surface: A question about a Scottish town that forbids noisy music.
explanation.walkthrough: Banff is a small coastal town in north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Banff is a town in Aberdeenshire, so it is somewhere Scots live.

clue.text: Little colour in a notably soft drink

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for an adjective: having little colour

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical notation for soft
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A soft drink with hardly any hue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notably' means 'in musical notation', so soft is P.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wan or faded has hardly any colour in it.

clue.text: Where an outstanding person turns up in Nevada

indicators.note: in a down answer, turns up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a oner is British slang for a remarkable, one-of-a-kind person

explanation.surface: A star appears somewhere in the Nevada desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the place clue 'Where... in Nevada': Reno is a city in that state.
explanation.definitionFit: Reno is a city in western Nevada, famous for casinos and quick divorces.

clue.text: Pretentious talk about a busybody

parts.note: c, circa, means about
the ant is the proverbial busy creature

explanation.surface: Pompous chatter concerning a meddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busybody' means a meddler in the surface; here it is a body that is busy, an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is hypocritical or sanctimonious jargon, empty talk.

clue.text: Artist's material discovered by F BI agents in a mine

indicators.note: in places the agents inside the mine word

parts.note: a pit is a mine
G-men are FBI agents, government men

explanation.surface: Federal agents uncover a painter's supplies down a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigment is the coloured powder from which paints are made.

clue.text: Beam from a mixed-up offspring in transport

indicators.note: in places the scrambled piece inside the transport word

parts.note: a tram is a form of transport

indicators.note: mixed-up says the letters of the word for offspring are scrambled

parts.note: a son is offspring

explanation.surface: A ray of light from a confused child riding a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' looks like a smile or ray of light; it is a structural crossbar. 'mixed-up' scrambles the offspring word before 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar or beam, as above a door or window.

clue.text: Cordial once, the clumsy animal smashes cars

parts.note: the hippo is a proverbially clumsy, lumbering animal

indicators.note: smashes means the letters of cars are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A heavy beast crashes into vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: Hippocras was a medieval drink of wine spiced and sweetened.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocras was a spiced wine drunk in past centuries, a historic sweet liqueur.

clue.text: Following coach

definitions.meaning: a following, a retinue of attendants
to coach is to instruct or school

explanation.definitionFit: A retinue trails behind a dignitary, and to coach someone is to school them.
